person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: auditory frequency representations in classically defined somatosensory cortex - whether responses to a non-preferred modality carry specific information
span.quote: Although the occurrence of multimodal responses in sensory cortex is no longer disputed, whether the responses to “non-preferred” modalities observed in sensory areas convey specific representations and how they relate to perception remain open questions.

span.label: whether parietal responses to sound are frequency-selective and related to perception, or merely present
span.quote: Even in cases where auditory stimulation has been shown to evoke distinct response signatures in somatosensory cortex ( Liang et al. 2013 ), it remains unclear whether these response patterns represent specific auditory information.

span.label: frequency-specific auditory responses in parietal cortex whose representational geometry correlates with offline perceptual similarity judgments, surviving conservative erosion of the parieto-temporal border
span.quote: Moreover, using representational similarity analysis to define the relationships between multi-voxel activation patterns for all sound pairs, we found clear similarity patterns for auditory responses in the parietal lobe that correlated significantly with perceptual similarity judgments. Our results demonstrate that auditory frequency representations can be distributed over brain regions traditionally considered to be dedicated to somatosensation.

span.label: existence
span.quote: Our results demonstrate that auditory frequency representations can be distributed over brain regions traditionally considered to be dedicated to somatosensation.

span.label: auditory frequency representation in somatosensory cortex
span.quote: Here we focus on temporal frequency processing in the human brain.

span.label: fmri
span.quote: In this functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) study, we measured BOLD signal changes in participants performing an auditory frequency discrimination task and characterized activation patterns related to stimulus frequency using both univariate and multivariate analysis approaches.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Sounds and vibrations that share frequency content co-occur constantly in everyday experience, and this long history of co-activation builds audio-tactile associations inside frequency-processing circuits
span.quote: The co-occurrence of auditory and somatosensory signals that are highly specific in the frequency domain may build audio-tactile associations in frequency-processing circuits through an extensive history of co-activation.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Predictive coding: hearing a tone evokes the neural representation of the tactile event usually associated with that tone, producing parietal activity with no mechanical stimulation at all
span.quote: In this framework, the auditory responses in parietal cortex could reflect predictive coding mechanisms in which hearing specific tones evokes neural representations of the tactile events associated with the sounds even in the absence of mechanical stimulation.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Auditory signals reach parietal cortex over already-documented cortico-cortical and thalamo-cortical routes linking the auditory and somatosensory systems
span.quote: Extensive cortico-cortical and thalamo-cortical pathways connecting the somatosensory and auditory systems have been identified using invasive tracing methods

span.label: subgroups of voxels in classically defined somatosensory regions of the parietal lobe respond to audition and are better suited to represent auditory frequency information
span.quote: These collective results indicate that auditory frequency representations in bilateral SR eroded are sensitive to ROI size and voxel inclusion criteria, unlike those in AR eroded which are more robust to the same criteria. Furthermore, the results for SR eroded imply that subgroups of voxels in classically defined somatosensory regions of the parietal lobe respond to audition and are better suited to represent auditory frequency information.

span.label: with the proposed route being an extensive history of co-activation at frequencies common to both senses, so that hearing a tone evokes the tactile representation associated with it
span.quote: The co-occurrence of auditory and somatosensory signals that are highly specific in the frequency domain may build audio-tactile associations in frequency-processing circuits through an extensive history of co-activation. In this framework, the auditory responses in parietal cortex could reflect predictive coding mechanisms in which hearing specific tones evokes neural representations of the tactile events associated with the sounds even in the absence of mechanical stimulation. Accordingly, parietal regions would only be responsive to a relatively low range of auditory frequencies which overlap those experienced through touch. This key prediction should be tested in future experiments.

span.label: and the association may be feature-specific - frequency shared between the senses where stimulus duration appears to rely on modality-dedicated circuits
span.quote: Interestingly, although common neural circuits may support frequency processing for audition and touch ( Butler et al. 2012 ), processing of other temporal features, like stimulus duration ( Butler et al. 2011 ), appears to rely on modality-dedicated circuits which implies that the neural associations between audition and touch may be feature-specific.

span.label: fMRI's temporal resolution cannot say whether the parietal auditory responses are feedforward or feedback.
span.note: what this limits: the direction of the parietal auditory signal: DUE TO THE LIMITED TEMPORAL RESOLUTION OF fMRI, IT IS UNCLEAR WHETHER THE AUDITORY RESPONSES IN PARIETAL CORTEX REFLECT FEEDFORWARD OR FEEDBACK SIGNALING
span.quote: Due to the limited temporal resolution of fMRI, it is unclear whether the auditory responses in parietal cortex reflect feedforward or feedback signaling.

span.label: the task performed during the discrimination scans, designed to ensure that participants attended to stimulus frequency, did not permit a sensitive analysis of auditory discrimination performance
span.note: what this limits: the analysis the discrimination scans could not support: THE TASK ... DESIGNED TO ENSURE THAT PARTICIPANTS ATTENDED TO STIMULUS FREQUENCY, DID NOT PERMIT A SENSITIVE ANALYSIS
span.quote: We took this approach because the task performed during the discrimination scans, which was designed to ensure that participants attended to stimulus frequency, did not permit a sensitive analysis of auditory discrimination performance.

span.label: these observations need to be confirmed in ultra-high resolution scanning and single-unit recording experiments testing a more comprehensive range of tones
span.note: what this limits: the whole set of observations: THESE OBSERVATIONS NEED TO BE CONFIRMED IN ULTRA-HIGH RESOLUTION SCANNING AND SINGLE-UNIT RECORDING EXPERIMENTS TESTING A MORE COMPREHENSIVE RANGE OF TONES
span.quote: These observations need to be confirmed in ultra-high resolution scanning and single-unit recording experiments testing a more comprehensive range of tones.

span.label: the perceptual measure is a group average collected offline from mostly different people, because the in-scanner task was not designed to yield a sensitive discrimination measure
span.note: what this limits: the brain-to-perception comparison: WE COMPARED THE CORTICAL DISSIMILARITY MEASURES TO THE PERCEPTUAL DISSIMILARITY JUDGMENTS TESTED OFFLINE AND AVERAGED across mostly different people
span.quote: Admittedly, our approach can be substantially improved in future studies. For instance, we compared the cortical dissimilarity measures to the perceptual dissimilarity judgments tested offline and averaged over subjects. We took this approach because the task performed during the discrimination scans, which was designed to ensure that participants attended to stimulus frequency, did not permit a sensitive analysis of auditory discrimination performance. Future experiments to confirm the relationship between parietal lobe responses and auditory perception should be designed to assess subject-specific and temporally-specific (i.e., trial-wise) associations.

span.label: auditory frequency representations in bilateral SR eroded are sensitive to ROI size and voxel inclusion criteria, unlike those in AR eroded which are more robust to the same criteria
span.note: what this limits: the SR result specifically: AUDITORY FREQUENCY REPRESENTATIONS IN BILATERAL SR ERODED ARE SENSITIVE TO ROI SIZE AND VOXEL INCLUSION CRITERIA, UNLIKE THOSE IN AR ERODED WHICH ARE MORE ROBUST
span.quote: These collective results indicate that auditory frequency representations in bilateral SR eroded are sensitive to ROI size and voxel inclusion criteria, unlike those in AR eroded which are more robust to the same criteria. Furthermore, the results for SR eroded imply that subgroups of voxels in classically defined somatosensory regions of the parietal lobe respond to audition and are better suited to represent auditory frequency information.

span.label: the elimination of the cutaneous-activation account rests partly on a comparison whose data are not shown
span.note: what this limits: the cutaneous-activation argument: it rests on a comparison of frequency response profiles whose data are not shown
span.quote: Second, if the sound-related responses were due to cutaneous activation, the bimodal response profile over auditory frequencies in SR eroded (Fig. 5 B ) would presumably be reflected in frequency response profiles associated with actual tactile stimulation. Notably, we find that tactile stimulation at vibration frequencies matching the sound frequencies tested in the auditory discrimination scans produced response profiles that clearly differed from the pattern observed with sounds (data not shown).

span.label: fMRI cannot say whether the parietal auditory responses are feedforward or feedback
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 0 - feedforward against feedback is not resolvable at this temporal resolution
span.quote: Due to the limited temporal resolution of fMRI, it is unclear whether the auditory responses in parietal cortex reflect feedforward or feedback signaling. Auditory inputs could conceivably reach somatosensory regions with relatively short latencies and laminar response profiles consistent with feedforward processing as is the case with somatosensory inputs to some auditory regions ( Schroeder and Foxe 2002 ). Alternatively, but not exclusively, the auditory responses in parietal regions could reflect feedback projections from frontal regions that support working memory and decision-making independent of sensory modality

span.label: and whether frequency is explicitly tuned, temporally coded or topographically arranged in somatosensory cortex is unknown
span.note: what this limits: any claim that somatosensory cortex represents frequency explicitly: EVIDENCE FOR EXPLICIT FREQUENCY TUNING is lacking, even where spike timing can signal vibration above 100 Hz
span.quote: In non-human primates, neurons in primary somatosensory cortex can signal vibration frequencies above 100 Hz in their spike timing ( Harvey et al. 2013 ), but evidence for explicit frequency tuning in somatosensory cortex remains elusive. Whether auditory information is similarly carried in somatosensory cortex using a temporal code is unknown.

span.label: the cortical DM calculated for each ROI compared to the group perceptual DM, so that a high correlation indicates the representational geometry of the auditory stimuli in the ROI corresponds to the geometry of the stimuli in perceptual space
span.quote: To relate neural and perceptual representations of the auditory frequencies, we compared the cortical DM calculated for each ROI to the group perceptual DM. We computed the Spearman correlation between the perceptual DM and each participant’s cortical DMs. A high correlation in these analyses would indicate that the representational geometry of the auditory stimuli in the ROI corresponds to the geometry of the stimuli in perceptual space.

span.label: pairwise similarity ratings, collected outside the scanner and turned into a dissimilarity matrix
span.quote: Admittedly, our approach can be substantially improved in future studies. For instance, we compared the cortical dissimilarity measures to the perceptual dissimilarity judgments tested offline and averaged over subjects. We took this approach because the task performed during the discrimination scans, which was designed to ensure that participants attended to stimulus frequency, did not permit a sensitive analysis of auditory discrimination performance. Future experiments to confirm the relationship between parietal lobe responses and auditory perception should be designed to assess subject-specific and temporally-specific (i.e., trial-wise) associations.

span.label: the 100 to 300 Hz range as the band where the two senses overlap, used to predict where parietal responses should stop
span.quote: The co-occurrence of auditory and somatosensory signals that are highly specific in the frequency domain may build audio-tactile associations in frequency-processing circuits through an extensive history of co-activation. In this framework, the auditory responses in parietal cortex could reflect predictive coding mechanisms in which hearing specific tones evokes neural representations of the tactile events associated with the sounds even in the absence of mechanical stimulation. Accordingly, parietal regions would only be responsive to a relatively low range of auditory frequencies which overlap those experienced through touch. This key prediction should be tested in future experiments.

span.label: temporal coding of vibration frequency in somatosensory cortex, named as the mechanism that would explain the fMRI result and has not been shown
span.quote: In non-human primates, neurons in primary somatosensory cortex can signal vibration frequencies above 100 Hz in their spike timing ( Harvey et al. 2013 ), but evidence for explicit frequency tuning in somatosensory cortex remains elusive. Whether auditory information is similarly carried in somatosensory cortex using a temporal code is unknown.

span.label: a +/-5 per cent JITTER added to the loudness-matched amplitude of every stimulus presentation
span.note: eliminates: amplitude as a systematic correlate of frequency - without it, a region that appeared to encode auditory FREQUENCY could be responding to loudness instead, which is the confound the paper's whole claim turns on · outcome: held
span.quote: To ensure that stimulus amplitude did not systematically vary with stimulus frequency, we introduced a jitter (±5%) to the loudness-matched amplitude levels on every stimulus presentation.

span.label: ROI size → statistical relationship
span.note: AN ANALYSIS CHOICE THAT MOVES THE RESULT: significant correlations required between 50 and 200 voxels with the tactile mask, and beyond that, including more voxels WEAKENED the relationship. The correlation is not a fixed property; it depends on where the ROI is cut.
span.quote: With SR eroded , significant correlations were attained with voxels from the auditory localizer mask for ROIs exceeding 130 voxels. In contrast, correlations between the perceptual and cortical DMs with the tactile and audio-tactile masks showed a stronger dependence on ROI size. With the tactile mask, significant correlations required between 50 and 200 voxels. Beyond this size, the inclusion of more voxels weakened the statistical relationship between the perceptual and cortical DMs. With the audio-tactile mask, significant correlations were only obtained with ROIs including 300–350 voxels.

span.label: cortical and perceptual DMs → postcentral gyrus
span.note: POSITIVE CORRELATION, RESTRICTED: significant only in the postcentral and supramarginal gyri, and only under the auditory mask. The restriction IS the result - an unscoped edge would assert it across parietal cortex, which the span explicitly denies.
span.quote: While positive relationships between the cortical and perceptual DMs were seen in nearly all of the bilateral parietal ROIs, significant correlations were only observed in the postcentral gyrus and the supramarginal gyrus (Fig. 8 ) and these significant patterns were only evident with the auditory mask. These results demonstrate that auditory representations in parietal cortex are not restricted to the higher-order somatosensory regions in close proximity to auditory cortex, as would be expected if the parietal responses were simply due to partial volume effects. Additionally, they confirm that the parietal lobe voxels that responded best to sounds in the localizer scans were the voxels most likely to represent auditory frequency information in a manner consistent with perception.

span.label: THE REGION'S NAME DOES NOT BOUND WHAT IT PROCESSES: robust and frequency-specific responses to sound in CLASSICALLY DEFINED somatosensory areas, against the traditional notion of modality-dedicated cortical systems
span.quote: Recent studies have challenged the traditional notion of modality-dedicated cortical systems by showing that audition and touch evoke responses in the same sensory brain regions. While much of this work has focused on somatosensory responses in auditory regions, fewer studies have investigated sound responses and representations in somatosensory regions. In this functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) study, we measured BOLD signal changes in participants performing an auditory frequency discrimination task and characterized activation patterns related to stimulus frequency using both univariate and multivariate analysis approaches. Outside of bilateral temporal lobe regions, we observed robust and frequency-specific responses to auditory stimulation in classically defined somatosensory areas.

span.label: and the question is sharpened before the measurement - multimodal responses are NO LONGER DISPUTED, but whether they convey SPECIFIC representations and how they relate to perception are the open questions
span.quote: Although the occurrence of multimodal responses in sensory cortex is no longer disputed, whether the responses to “non-preferred” modalities observed in sensory areas convey specific representations and how they relate to perception remain open questions.

span.label: with the precise gap named: auditory stimulation was already known to evoke distinct signatures in somatosensory cortex, and it REMAINED UNCLEAR whether those patterns represent specific auditory information
span.quote: Even in cases where auditory stimulation has been shown to evoke distinct response signatures in somatosensory cortex ( Liang et al. 2013 ), it remains unclear whether these response patterns represent specific auditory information.

span.label: WHICH LOCALIZER DEFINED THE VOXELS IS ITSELF THE HYPOTHESIS TEST: separate auditory, tactile and audio-tactile masks, used to ask whether parietal voxels PRIVILEGED in their sensitivity to sound are the ones that carry the representation
span.quote: By separately identifying voxels responsive to auditory, tactile, or combined audio-tactile stimulation in the localizer scans, we determined whether parietal lobe voxels exhibited selectivity for sensory modalities or responded to both auditory and tactile stimulation. This then enabled us to test whether auditory frequency representations were more likely to be supported by parietal lobe voxels that were privileged in their sensitivity to auditory inputs.

span.label: AND THE ANSWER DEPENDS ON THE MASK: fewer and smaller regions show a frequency effect with the tactile mask, and the paper reads that difference as the result rather than as noise
span.quote: The differences in the results acquired with the tactile localizer masks compared to the auditory and audio-tactile masks imply that brain regions preferentially responsive to auditory stimulation in the localizer scans were more likely to exhibit significant response modulation related to auditory frequency.

span.label: THE SAME DATA ARE SIGNIFICANT OR NULL BY MASK, ONCE SPLIT BY HEMISPHERE: in the left somatosensory ROI the auditory mask gives r = 0.24 P < 0.05, the tactile mask r = 0.07 P = 0.25 and the audio-tactile mask r = 0.1 P = 0.15
span.quote: In contrast, separating the data according to hemisphere disrupted the relationship between the multivariate representations in SR eroded and the perceptual DM for some of the masks. Although the positive correlation between frequency distance and pattern dissimilarity remained for the somatosensory ROI in the left and right hemispheres with all masks (Fig. 7 A ), the correlation achieved statistical significance only with the auditory masks (auditory LH : mean r = 0.24, W = 45, P < 0.05; tactile LH : mean r = 0.07; W = 34; P = 0.25; audio-tactile LH : mean r = 0.1; W = 38; P = 0.15; auditory RH : mean r = 0.37, W = 54, P < 0.002; tactile mask RH : mean r = 0.18; W = 41; P = 0.1; audio-tactile mask RH : mean r = 0.18; W = 46; P < 0.05).

span.label: and the same split against perception - significant correlations ONLY with the auditory masks, with the tactile left-hemisphere mask at P = 0.07
span.quote: Accordingly, significant correlations between the left and right SR eroded cortical DMs and the perceptual DM were observed only with the auditory masks (Fig. 7 B ) (auditory LH : mean r = 0.31, W = 54, P < 0.002; tactile LH : mean r = 0.12; W = 42.5; P = 0.07; audio-tactile LH : mean r = 0.12; W = 37; P = 0.2; auditory RH : mean r = 0.35, W = 54, P < 0.002; tactile mask RH : mean r = 0.2; W = 45; P < 0.05; audio-tactile mask RH : mean r = 0.16; W = 42.5; P = 0.07).

span.label: THE RESULT EXISTS INSIDE A WINDOW OF ANALYSIS SIZE, AND THE WINDOW DIFFERS BY MASK: the auditory mask needs more than 130 voxels, the tactile mask between 50 and 200 - BEYOND WHICH MORE VOXELS WEAKEN IT - and the audio-tactile mask only 300 to 350
span.quote: With SR eroded , significant correlations were attained with voxels from the auditory localizer mask for ROIs exceeding 130 voxels. In contrast, correlations between the perceptual and cortical DMs with the tactile and audio-tactile masks showed a stronger dependence on ROI size. With the tactile mask, significant correlations required between 50 and 200 voxels. Beyond this size, the inclusion of more voxels weakened the statistical relationship between the perceptual and cortical DMs. With the audio-tactile mask, significant correlations were only obtained with ROIs including 300–350 voxels.

span.label: stated plainly as a limit - the parietal representations are SENSITIVE to ROI size and voxel inclusion criteria where the temporal ones are ROBUST to the same criteria
span.quote: These collective results indicate that auditory frequency representations in bilateral SR eroded are sensitive to ROI size and voxel inclusion criteria, unlike those in AR eroded which are more robust to the same criteria. Furthermore, the results for SR eroded imply that subgroups of voxels in classically defined somatosensory regions of the parietal lobe respond to audition and are better suited to represent auditory frequency information.

span.label: A THRESHOLD CHOSEN FOR ITS ROLE IN THE PIPELINE, NOT FOR INFERENCE: a LIBERAL uncorrected P < 0.05 used to build the masks, precisely because they only constrain later tests
span.quote: Because we intended to use these response patterns to constrain the univariate analyses of the auditory discrimination scans, we used a liberal threshold P < 0.05 (uncorrected) to generate separate masks for the auditory, tactile, and audio-tactile conditions

span.label: THE artifact IS ELIMINATED BY A PARAMETRIC SWEEP RATHER THAN ONE CONTROL: ROIs eroded by 2 mm, then 4 mm, then 10 mm - and the auditory-mask result survives all three
span.quote: In control analyses, we repeated the RSA using more extreme erosion levels ( Supplementary Fig. 1 ) and found nearly identical results with ROIs eroded by 4 mm. RSA with the auditory mask revealed significant auditory representations in somatosensory regions even when performed on a ROI eroded by 10 mm ( Supplementary Fig. 1 ). These supplementary analyses confirm that auditory information can be represented in parietal cortex even when the perisylvian regions most susceptible to partial volume effects or spatial blurring artifacts, particularly those in the parietal operculum, are excluded.

span.label: with four separate design decisions listed against the same confound - 2 mm isotropic voxels, no volumetric smoothing, surface-space filtering, and conservative borders
span.quote: We addressed this concern in multiple ways. First, we acquired our data in 2-mm isotropic voxels and we avoided spatial smoothing while maintaining the data in native volume space whenever possible. Second, when we spatially filtered or sampled our data, we performed these operations in surface space rather than volume space to reduce cross-fissure contamination. Third, we carefully inspected the spatial response profiles in the parietal operculum to confirm the presence of auditory responses far from the areal boundaries (Fig. 2 ). Fourth, we adopted conservative ROI border definitions that minimized the inclusion of ambiguous voxels.

span.label: AND THE SPATIAL ARGUMENT IS TURNED AROUND: the significant parietal subdivisions are NOT the ones closest to auditory cortex, which is what a partial-volume account would have required
span.quote: While positive relationships between the cortical and perceptual DMs were seen in nearly all of the bilateral parietal ROIs, significant correlations were only observed in the postcentral gyrus and the supramarginal gyrus (Fig. 8 ) and these significant patterns were only evident with the auditory mask. These results demonstrate that auditory representations in parietal cortex are not restricted to the higher-order somatosensory regions in close proximity to auditory cortex, as would be expected if the parietal responses were simply due to partial volume effects. Additionally, they confirm that the parietal lobe voxels that responded best to sounds in the localizer scans were the voxels most likely to represent auditory frequency information in a manner consistent with perception.

span.label: ONE CONTROL EXPERIMENT ANSWERING TWO DIFFERENT OBJECTIONS: air-conduction headphones show the effect does not need vibrating earbuds, AND that session involved no touch at all, so a learned sound-vibration association cannot explain it either
span.quote: Lastly, in control fMRI experiments designed specifically to test whether vibrating earbud elements are required for sound-related parietal activations we found that significant BOLD signal changes in parietal brain regions can be achieved using sound stimuli delivered via circumaural, air-conduction headphones ( Supplementary Fig. 2 ). Collectively, our main and Supplementary data suggest that the activation patterns we observe in parietal cortex relate to auditory processing. Importantly, the control fMRI experiment also served to demonstrate that auditory responses could be observed in parietal regions even in scan sessions that involved no tactile stimulation. This addresses concerns that the auditory activations in somatosensory cortex during the main experiments resulted from a rapidly learned association between the sounds and vibrations experienced during the localizer and discrimination scans.

span.label: and the earbud account is refuted by SOMATOTOPY - cutaneous drive in the ear canal would confine the response to the ear representation, and the responses are broadly distributed
span.quote: Second, we addressed the concern that the parietal responses to auditory stimulation reflected tactile processing explicitly. Specifically, because the MRI-compatible in-ear headphones used in the fMRI scans produce sounds via vibrating piezoelectric elements, cutaneous receptors in the ear canal may have been mechanically driven by the earbuds to produce the responses in somatosensory regions. A number of considerations argue against this concern. First, because of the somatotopic organization of the somatosensory system in parietal cortex, the sound-induced activation patterns would presumably be spatially constrained to only the ear representations if they were associated with cutaneous receptor activation in the ear canal. Our data indicate that auditory responses are broadly distributed over the parietal lobe.

span.label: A LOAD-BEARING COMPARISON WHOSE EVIDENCE IS NOT IN THE PAPER: tactile stimulation at matched frequencies gave response profiles that 'clearly differed' from the sound profiles - DATA NOT SHOWN
span.quote: Second, if the sound-related responses were due to cutaneous activation, the bimodal response profile over auditory frequencies in SR eroded (Fig. 5 B ) would presumably be reflected in frequency response profiles associated with actual tactile stimulation. Notably, we find that tactile stimulation at vibration frequencies matching the sound frequencies tested in the auditory discrimination scans produced response profiles that clearly differed from the pattern observed with sounds (data not shown).

span.label: TWO NEGATIVE CONTROLS, ONE ACROSS REGIONS AND ONE WITHIN: visual cortex patterns do not correlate with the perceptual geometry, and neither do the voxels that DEACTIVATED in the localizer
span.quote: In (negative) control analyses, we performed RSA on multivariate patterns measured in a visual cortex region ( Supplementary Fig. 3 ) and failed to find significant correlations between the cortical representational spaces and the perceptual DM. Thus, the relationship between cortical and perceptual DMs for the auditory stimuli tested in our experiments appears to be specific to temporal and parietal cortex.

span.label: THE TWO SIDES OF THE CORRELATION COME FROM DIFFERENT PEOPLE AND DIFFERENT SESSIONS: the perceptual judgments were collected offline and averaged over subjects, because the in-scanner task could not yield a sensitive discrimination measure
span.quote: Admittedly, our approach can be substantially improved in future studies. For instance, we compared the cortical dissimilarity measures to the perceptual dissimilarity judgments tested offline and averaged over subjects. We took this approach because the task performed during the discrimination scans, which was designed to ensure that participants attended to stimulus frequency, did not permit a sensitive analysis of auditory discrimination performance. Future experiments to confirm the relationship between parietal lobe responses and auditory perception should be designed to assess subject-specific and temporally-specific (i.e., trial-wise) associations.

span.label: and the peak sits at the edge of the tested range - the somatosensory profile is bimodal with a peak at 75 Hz, THE LOWEST TESTED FREQUENCY
span.quote: Furthermore, response profiles over the stimulus frequencies were similar across hemispheres and localizer masks (Fig. 5 B ), although these profiles differed slightly between AR eroded and SR eroded . Specifically, in both regions qualitatively larger responses were centered on 200 Hz, but the bimodally distributed responses in SR eroded also contained a peak at 75 Hz, the lowest tested frequency.

span.quote: With the auditory localizer mask, we found that auditory stimulation during the discrimination scans, collapsed over frequency conditions, was associated with significant signal modulation (FDR q < 0.05) in 37 and 54 clusters spanning the left and right hemispheres, respectively

span.label: mean r = 0.40, W = 54, P < 0.005 — relationship between frequency distance and activation-pattern dissimilarity in the bilateral somatosensory ROI with the auditory localizer mask
span.quote: significant positive relationships were evident with all masks (auditory mask: mean r = 0.40, W = 54, P < 0.005; tactile mask: mean r = 0.24; W = 45; P < 0.05; audio-tactile mask: mean r = 0.25; W = 45; P < 0.05)

span.label: mean r = 0.41, W = 55, P < 0.001 — correlation between the perceptual dissimilarity matrix and the somatosensory-ROI cortical dissimilarity matrix with the auditory mask
span.quote: although there tended to be stronger correlations with the auditory mask (auditory mask: mean r = 0.41, W = 55, P < 0.001; tactile mask: mean r = 0.22; W = 46; P < 0.05; audio-tactile mask: mean r = 0.21; W = 45; P < 0.05)

span.label: mean r = 0.83, W = 21, P < 0.05 — relationship between perceptual similarity ratings and absolute frequency differences between tones
span.quote: This relationship between perceptual similarity ratings and absolute differences in stimulus frequency was positive and significant (mean r = 0.83, W = 21, P < 0.05).

span.label: 0.49 ± 0.012 — chance-level tactile detection rate when subjects had no physical contact with the stimulator, confirming the tactile stimuli were inaudible
span.quote: In control experiments performed in the scanner, participants achieved only chance-level performance on a tactile detection task in the absence of physical contact with the tactile stimulator (mean detection rate: 0.49 ± 0.012)

span.label: 130 voxels — ROI size the eroded somatosensory region had to exceed before perceptual-cortical correlations reached significance with the auditory mask
span.quote: With SR eroded , significant correlations were attained with voxels from the auditory localizer mask for ROIs exceeding 130 voxels.

span.label: r = 0.24 ... r = 0.07 ... r = 0.1 — the same somatosensory data analysed with three different localizer masks - one significant, two not, so the mask decides whether there is a finding
span.quote: In contrast, separating the data according to hemisphere disrupted the relationship between the multivariate representations in SR eroded and the perceptual DM for some of the masks. Although the positive correlation between frequency distance and pattern dissimilarity remained for the somatosensory ROI in the left and right hemispheres with all masks (Fig. 7 A ), the correlation achieved statistical significance only with the auditory masks (auditory LH : mean r = 0.24, W = 45, P < 0.05; tactile LH : mean r = 0.07; W = 34; P = 0.25; audio-tactile LH : mean r = 0.1; W = 38; P = 0.15; auditory RH : mean r = 0.37, W = 54, P < 0.002; tactile mask RH : mean r = 0.18; W = 41; P = 0.1; audio-tactile mask RH : mean r = 0.18; W = 46; P < 0.05).

span.label: 130 ... 50 and 200 ... 300–350 — the ROI sizes at which each mask yields a significant brain-perception correlation, with the tactile mask WEAKENING beyond its window - a result that exists only inside an analysis-size range
span.quote: With SR eroded , significant correlations were attained with voxels from the auditory localizer mask for ROIs exceeding 130 voxels. In contrast, correlations between the perceptual and cortical DMs with the tactile and audio-tactile masks showed a stronger dependence on ROI size. With the tactile mask, significant correlations required between 50 and 200 voxels. Beyond this size, the inclusion of more voxels weakened the statistical relationship between the perceptual and cortical DMs. With the audio-tactile mask, significant correlations were only obtained with ROIs including 300–350 voxels.

span.label: 10 mm — the most extreme erosion of the parieto-temporal border at which the auditory-mask result still holds - a parametric sweep on the artifact rather than a single control
span.quote: In control analyses, we repeated the RSA using more extreme erosion levels ( Supplementary Fig. 1 ) and found nearly identical results with ROIs eroded by 4 mm. RSA with the auditory mask revealed significant auditory representations in somatosensory regions even when performed on a ROI eroded by 10 mm ( Supplementary Fig. 1 ). These supplementary analyses confirm that auditory information can be represented in parietal cortex even when the perisylvian regions most susceptible to partial volume effects or spatial blurring artifacts, particularly those in the parietal operculum, are excluded.

span.label: 0.49 — detection of the tactile stimulator without physical contact - chance, which is what licenses treating the vibrations as inaudible
span.quote: First, we confirmed that the tactile stimuli used during the fMRI scans were inaudible to the subjects in control experiments. This confirmation is important because the distinction between the auditory and tactile analysis masks would be confounded if the vibrations occurring on the fingers were explicitly associated with sounds. In control experiments performed in the scanner, participants achieved only chance-level performance on a tactile detection task in the absence of physical contact with the tactile stimulator (mean detection rate: 0.49 ± 0.012)—presumably, performance would have been better had the subjects been able to hear the vibrations.

span.label: 75 Hz — the second peak of the somatosensory frequency profile, and also the lowest frequency tested - so the profile's shape is bounded by the design
span.quote: Furthermore, response profiles over the stimulus frequencies were similar across hemispheres and localizer masks (Fig. 5 B ), although these profiles differed slightly between AR eroded and SR eroded . Specifically, in both regions qualitatively larger responses were centered on 200 Hz, but the bimodally distributed responses in SR eroded also contained a peak at 75 Hz, the lowest tested frequency.
